cases.label: case-only variants 'Us', 'uS' and 'us ' of a country code join 'US'
cases.reasoning: CI_AS ignores case and SQL Server equality ignores trailing spaces, so all three province codes join country 'US'. The conversion uses rtrim under an ICU level-2 collation; this checks mixed case and case plus trailing space together.

cases.label: expansions: province code 'Æ' against country 'AE' and 'ß' against 'SS', with 'ae' and 'ss' as case-only controls
cases.reasoning: Windows collation rules (used by SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS for nvarchar) treat 'Æ' as equal to 'AE' and 'ß' as equal to 'ss'. The ICU root collation at strength 2 gives 'æ' its own primary weight (not equal to 'ae') while 'ß' = 'ss' differs only at the tertiary level. The engines may disagree on whether the 'Æ' province joins.

cases.label: compatibility forms: full-width U+FF35 U+FF33 against 'US' and the Kelvin sign U+212A followed by 'E' against 'KE', with 'ke' as a case-only control
cases.reasoning: SQL Server collations without _WS are width-insensitive, so full-width 'ＵＳ' equals 'US'; U+212A KELVIN SIGN is canonically equivalent to 'K'. ICU at strength 2 ignores width (a tertiary difference) and normalises canonical equivalents. Either engine may treat one of these differently.

cases.label: whitespace look-alikes: 'US' with a trailing no-break space (U+00A0), a trailing tab, a leading space, a soft hyphen (U+00AD) inside, and 'CA ' (a real trailing space)
cases.reasoning: SQL Server pads the shorter value with U+0020 before comparing, so only 'CA ' is certain to join. Whether U+00A0 compares equal to the pad space, and whether the soft hyphen U+00AD is ignorable, are collation rules; PostgreSQL rtrim(' ') removes U+0020 only and ICU treats U+00AD as ignorable and U+00A0 as a space variant. A tab and a leading space should join on neither engine.

cases.label: accents and dotted/dotless I: 'ÜS' against 'US' (accent-sensitive); U+0131 and U+0130 followed by 'T' against 'IT', with 'it' as a case-only control
cases.reasoning: CI_AS is accent-sensitive, so 'ÜS' must not join 'US'. U+0131 (dotless i) and U+0130 (I with dot above) case-fold differently by rule set: Windows rules and ICU root may each match or not match 'IT'. 'it' joins on both.

cases.label: an empty country code: province codes '' and ' ' both join country '' (trailing spaces ignored)
cases.reasoning: SQL Server compares '' and ' ' as equal (padding), so both provinces join the country whose code is ''. rtrim(' ') gives '' on PostgreSQL; this checks the empty-string edge of the rtrim + ICU equality and that '' is not treated as NULL.

cases.label: NULL versus '' in every nullable text column: Title, MiddleName, Suffix, AddressLine2, EmailAddress; an email row whose address is NULL
cases.reasoning: Each nullable column is sent once as NULL and once as ''. SQL Server keeps '' distinct from NULL (no ANSI_NULLS or concatenation is involved); a conversion or driver that turned '' into NULL (or the reverse) would differ. Person 3 has an EmailAddress row with a NULL address, which must look the same as person 1's missing row.

null-vs-empty.detail: empty string: yes; NULL in a text input: yes

cases.label: text returned as stored: trailing spaces, values differing only in case, non-ASCII and an emoji, full-length nvarchar values
cases.reasoning: Names 'Ann', 'ANN' and 'ann ' come back with their own spelling and trailing space (nvarchar keeps trailing spaces; no comparison applies). An emoji (a surrogate pair in UTF-16), combining characters and a 50-character LastName check the nvarchar -> varchar mapping and the load on both engines.

cases.label: two identical phone rows, two phones of one type and an unknown phone type: one row per phone, duplicates kept
cases.reasoning: PersonPhone has no key constraint in the scratch tables, so the same (person, number, type) twice gives two identical output rows; the view has no DISTINCT. A third phone of type 9 has no PhoneNumberType row (LEFT JOIN: NULL). Rows are compared as a multiset.

top-ties.detail: two rows of Person.PersonPhone share BusinessEntityID = 1

cases.label: keys with gaps and at the int limits: employees 0, 7 and 2147483647, address -2147483648; one address shared by two employees
cases.reasoning: BusinessEntityID and AddressID are keys; values jump (0, 7, 2147483647) and include the int minimum. Two employees share address -2147483648, so the address row is used twice.

cases.label: xml passed through: a default namespace, escaped & and <, attributes, an empty element, a fragment with two roots, and text-only content
cases.reasoning: AdditionalContactInfo is xml on both engines and passed through. The documents are written in SQL Server's serialised form (double-quoted attributes, & and < escaped, empty elements as <x/>), so any difference comes from the engines: SQL Server stores xml in a binary form and re-serialises it, PostgreSQL keeps the text. Fragments and text-only content are valid xml in both.

objections.text: The hand-derived fixed cases already test a lowercase province code joining 'US' under CI_AS and a province code with a trailing space joining 'US'. Using additional mixed-case spellings and combining case with the trailing space attacks the same two join mechanisms.
A09 inserts the identical PersonPhone primary-key tuple (BusinessEntityID 1, PhoneNumber '555-0100', PhoneNumberTypeID 1) twice. That duplicate cannot occur under the source schema preconditions.
